newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to get $400 mln in ADB loans for 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to get $400 mln in ADB loans for 1996/97.

text.p: Bangladesh will receive $400 million in loans from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in 1996/97 (July-June), which is $170 million more than the previous year, Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said on Friday.

ADB assistance to Bangladesh fell to $166 million in 1994/95 due to a "cooling off" in relations between the bank and the then government under former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia, the official BSS news agency quoted Kibria as saying.
He did not elaborate, but Finance Ministry officials said the cooling off occurred because the ADB felt Khaleda's government was slow and inefficient in using foreign assistance.
Kibria was speaking to reporters on his return from Japan where he attended a meeting of the ADB board of governors.
The ADB is one of Bangladesh's major aid donors.
Kibria said Japan would separately provide $130 million worth of loans for the 1996/97 year.
"I am very pleased to say that the shadow which was hanging over relations between Bangladesh and major bilateral donors is being removed successfully," BSS quoted the minister as saying.
